text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
IZVESTIA
- Local authorities in Primoriye, Russia's Far Eastern region, are sabotaging an anti-crisis programme prepared by the federal government, the paper says.
- Workers of the Rostov atomic power station in southern Russia attacked an environmentalists' group which picketed construction of the station.
- It is not clear how the rouble denomination announced on August 4 will affect Russians' personal accounts which were devalued in the early 90s when economic reforms started.
KOMMERSANT DAILY
- Up to the very last moment it was not clear whether Norilsky Nikel auction would take place.
- Russia's Central Bank started audits in commercial banks authorised to deal with the federal budget money. Uneximbank is the first to be checked.
- Russians are actively buying U.S. dollars after announcement of the rouble denomination, but the Central Bank is confident that rouble will not fall.
- Indonesia decided to buy 12 Russian Su-30 fighters and 8 Mi-17-1B helicopters instead of 9 U.S. bombers.
- The future of Russia's space industry depends on the success of the Mir orbital station repair mission which was launched yesterday.
- Small investors want to sell off shares of RAO Norilsky Nikel.
SEVODNYA
- Uneximbank used all of its legal and competetive advantages to win the Norilsk Nikel auction.
- Different social groups in Russia reacted differently to the news about denomination.
- Russian commercial banks will have to invest in industry in order to survive.
- Russia's State Tax Service is pessimistic about the country's economy.
- Moscow can expect further confrontation with the regions over privatisation of state assets.
NEZAVISIMAYA GAZETA
- Uneximbank's victory at the Norilsk Nikel auction is likely to cause a new round in the banking war.
- Communists will use the army issue in their new attack on the authorities which they plan this autunm. ROSSIISKIYE VESTI
- President Boris Yeltsin who has returned to Moscow after his summer holidays faces a lot of urgent state problems and unresolved political problems.
ROSSIISKAYA GAZETA
- Russia has neither money nor experience to develop rich gas and oil offshore deposits near Sakhalin Island, says Sakhalin's governor.
PRAVDA
- Scandals around privatisation will have an impact on the 2000 presidential elections, says the opposition paper.
MOSKOVSKY KOMSOMOLETS
- Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin gave up his seemingly neutral position in the banking war over privatisation of state assets.
-- Svetlana Kovaleva, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
